title: Compact Atelier: Performance Tiles & Microcharts for Per-Model/Per-Route Views
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Design a compact, reusable ‘Atelier Tile’ component set for per-model and per-route performance pages. Each tile is a self-contained micro-dashboard presenting latency distribution, throughput trend, and token composition in a space-efficient layout suitable for grid views and single-route detail panes. The tiles should scale from 200x120 px (compact) to 480x260 px (expanded) and include progressive reveal interactions for deeper microtraces. This ticket captures specs, visual assets, trade-offs, and rollout checks for an initial prototype and design review.
acceptance_criteria: Three canonical tile variants (compact, regular, expanded) with annotated specs checked into Figma
Chart behavior documented for latency (distribution), throughput (time-series), and token composition (stacked mini-bars), including sample data shapes
Interaction patterns (hover expand, click-to-open detail flyout, keyboard equivalents) implemented in the prototype
Accessibility checks documented (contrast ratios, ARIA labels, screen-reader ordering) and a11y owner assigned
Hand-off artifacts: tokens, spacing, chart color tokens, and example queries for backend engineers
design_notes: We introduced the Atelier metaphor to emphasize modularity: tiles can be rearranged into dashboards or tiled across route lists. Core constraints: keep perceptual load low in dense lists, preserve comparability across tiles (same scales or explicit percentile markers), and avoid expensive realtime queries by designing for pre-aggregated vectors (1m/5m buckets) with sparklines for near-real-time impressions.
chart_specs: Latency distribution (primary): compact violin-like mini-histogram with median/95th percentile markers. Data: bucketed latencies (20 buckets per minute). Visual: grayscale histogram bars with accent lines for p50/p95. Interaction: hover shows tooltip with numeric values and sample traces link.

Throughput sparkline (secondary): area+line sparkline representing requests/minute over last 60m, with thin baseline to save vertical space. Data: minute-level counts. Interaction: hover reveals peak minute value; click toggles small overlay showing average concurrency estimate.

Token composition stacked bars (tertiary): two-segment micro-bar showing prompt vs completion token ratio for the selected time window (defaults to last 60m). When expanded, the bar becomes a small histogram of token-length buckets. Visual: prompt=muted blue, completion=muted green. Tooltip shows absolute and relative token counts and per-token cost estimate.

Microtrace preview (expanded): when tile is expanded, show a condensed timeline of the top 3 slow traces (timestamp, model variant, top-level op durations). The trace view is a simplified waterfall (no deep span list) and links to the full trace in Observability.
Cost overlay (optional): a subtle per-tile cost estimate computed from tokens*unit_price; hidden under a cost toggle. Shown only to roles with billing visibility.
interactions: Compact: immediate hover reveals brief tooltip (latency p50/p95, throughput minute peak)
Hover-Expand: long-hover or keyboard focus expands to regular tile (accessibility: Enter/Space to expand).
Click: tile opens detail flyout anchored to tile with expanded charts and correlation controls (model variant selector, route filter).
Keyboard: tab order follows tile visual order; expanded flyout traps focus and returns focus to tile on close.
Progressive disclosure: heavy queries (microtraces, full histograms) load only after user expansion to limit backend cost.
data_model: Frontend receives a compact payload: {series: {latency_buckets: [20 ints], throughput: [60 ints], tokens: {prompt:int, completion:int}, top_traces: [{id, ts, dur_ms, variant}]}}. Backend preaggregates into 1m buckets; sampling for traces capped at 3 samples per minute per route. Example API path: /api/v1/console/routes/{route_id}/tile-metrics?window=60m&resolution=1m
decisions: Use percentile markers (p50, p95) instead of full scaled y-axis in compact view to preserve visual comparability across tiles.
Prefer pre-aggregated 1m buckets to minimize realtime load; use sampling for traces to keep cost low.
Expose cost only behind billing permission to avoid surprising users; default state is hidden.
Single-source color tokens will be used across console; muted palette chosen to avoid attention theft from route status badges.
risks: Sampling traces may obscure tail behaviors for small-volume routes; mitigation: add user-facing note and link to full trace search.
Compact charts can mislead if scales vary; mitigation: annotate when tile uses an independent scale and provide a toggle for unified scaling in dashboard mode.
Rendering many SVGs in route lists could affect client perf; mitigation: use canvas fallback and virtualization in long lists.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (internal): soft-launch on internal accounts and staging console for QA + perf measurement (2 weeks).
Stage 2 (canary): enable for 5% of production accounts with low-to-mid traffic routes to validate backend load and UX metrics (4 weeks).
Stage 3 (gradual): enable by default with telemetry events collected for engagement and misinterpretation signals; provide opt-out for users.
metrics_to_monitor: Backend: additional QPS and read amplification for /tile-metrics endpoint
Frontend: tile render time (ms), jank/frame in long lists
UX: click-through to detail flyout rate, hover-expansion rate, false-positive misread reports from support channels
Business: estimated incremental cost attributed to tile queries (USD/day) vs. instrumented value (engagement)
